terra.problem: Saying Ziklag was not pulled apart rules out damage the text does not address.
The passage does not say these events happened at night.
The text does not say whether David already had a plan.
Saying David inquires before doing anything else overlooks what he has already done, including asking for the ephod.
The claim that the town can wait because the captives cannot adds a reason the passage does not give.
The comparison implies the men traveled all night, but the passage gives no such timing.
The passage does not say that nobody was tied up. It simply does not mention tying up the Egyptian.
The Egyptian says his master was an Amalekite, but does not say his master was part of the raiding party.
The text does not say the Egyptian did not run off. It says his master abandoned him when he fell ill.
The text describes the Amalekites celebrating, but does not say they were confident.
The passage describes the Amalekites celebrating, but does not establish that nobody was asleep.
The text does not say that none of the Amalekites were packing.
The text says four hundred fled on camels, not how fast they got away.
David addresses the men who want to withhold the plunder as his brothers, not the two hundred who stayed behind. The explanation blurs that distinction.
This is a flat restatement of the verse, with no distinctive Papa Dorin voice in a moment that could hold some playful energy.
The narrator calls the elders David's friends. David does not call them that in his message.
The explanation is a flat sequence of restatements and quotations, without Papa Dorin's warmth or personality.
